subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The prescribed fix requires ADDING a live_preview block to the options object (live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: process.env.CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || '' }) and adding CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN to the env destructuring. This diff does the exact opposite — it REMOVES the live_preview block and the CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN env var. Without this config, the Contentstack SDK cannot detect preview mode or return draft entries. None of the verification criteria can be met.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-add CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN to the env destructuring block (lines 23-36) and re-add the live_preview block to the options object: live_preview: { enable: Boolean(CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN), preview_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN }.

issues.description: The prescribed fix requires importing and initializing ContentstackLivePreview from @contentstack/live-preview-utils with an onEntryChange callback that re-fetches changed entries and pushes them into React state. This diff REMOVES the entire initLivePreview function, the ContentstackLivePreview import, the onEntryChange callback, and the client-side re-fetch logic. No live preview pipeline exists after this change — the setContent field on the context interface is dead code with no producer.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-add the ContentstackLivePreview.init() call with stackSdk: Stack and an onEntryChange callback that re-fetches the changed entry using getSingleEntry/getSingletonEntry and pushes it into context via setContent or the page setter bridge.

issues.description: The prescribed fix requires adding an updater mechanism (setContent or setPage callback) to IContentstackContext so onEntryChange in _app.tsx can push updated entry data. While setContent is added to the interface, the module-level bridge that connected the _app.tsx onEntryChange callback to the per-page ContentstackContext.Provider (registerContentstackPageSetter, pushContentstackPageUpdate, getCurrentContentstackPageContext) is REMOVED entirely. With both the bridge removed and no ContentstackLivePreview initialization, setContent is never called by any live preview mechanism — it is dead code.
issues.suggestedFix: Either restore the module-level bridge pattern or implement the setContent callback wiring so that onEntryChange in _app.tsx can actually push updated entries into the context. The interface change alone is insufficient without the producer pipeline.

issues.description: The @contentstack/live-preview-utils dependency is REMOVED from package.json. The prescribed fix requires this package for ContentstackLivePreview.init() and onEntryChange(). Without it, the live preview SDK cannot be imported or used.

This file is NOT named in the prescribed plan. The diff removes the useState/useEffect page setter registration and directly accesses content?.page[0] with optional chaining, but then accesses error_image[0].public_id and error_image[0].format WITHOUT any null check. If content.page is empty or error_image is missing, this will throw a runtime TypeError. The previous code safely destructured from page[0] || ({} as I404).
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the null-safe pattern: const { title, error_copy, error_heading, error_image, homepage_cta } = content?.page?.[0] || ({} as I404); and guard imageUrl with: const imageUrl = error_image?.[0] ? `${error_image[0].public_id}.${error_image[0].format}` : "";

issues.description: This file is NOT named in the prescribed plan. The diff removes the useState/useEffect page setter registration and local page state management. While this simplifies the code, it removes the reactive state that would receive live preview updates. Since the prescribed fix requires onEntryChange to push updates into context, removing local state management from page components means the ContentstackContext.Provider value is now static (set once from server props and never updated).
issues.suggestedFix: If the setContent bridge pattern is restored in contentstackContext.tsx and _app.tsx, ensure page components either use local state that receives updates or that the Provider value is made reactive through the context itself.
